findings.title: A raw prehash signer would become a generic identity-key signing oracle
findings.summary: Authorizing service-net while accepting a caller-chosen 32-byte digest does not constrain key use: compromised or confused service-net code could obtain arbitrary protocol signatures under the durable relay identity. KMS and the protected root must construct the exact TLS 1.3 client CertificateVerify input from a typed request.

evidence.label: Dangerous sink
evidence.explanation: The current reference API signs any supplied prehash.
evidence.excerpt: pub fn sign(&self, digest: &[u8; 32]) -> Result<SigDer, SiloError>

evidence.label: Broken control
evidence.explanation: Caller identity limits who invokes the method, not what is signed.

evidence.label: Required change
evidence.explanation: Use a typed TLS13ClientCertificateVerify request containing active certificate/key generation, fixed ECDSA_P256_SHA256 scheme, client role, and transcript hash. KMS/provider constructs and hashes the standard TLS context internally. Expose no generic sign, raw key-id selection, or generic SPI signing command.

optionalProperties.phase_gate: Contract gate fails unless cross-protocol and malformed role/scheme/generation vectors deny, and the returned signature is self-verified against the active key.

findings.title: Local caller identity is not hardware attestation; AP-to-RoT trust is otherwise circular
findings.summary: The kernel trailer proves local scheduler origin assuming a trusted kernel; it carries no code measurement or secure-boot proof. A SPI signer that accepts the AP's assertion of attested KMS lets a compromised AP authorize itself, while a substituted bus endpoint can bypass local KMS policy.

locations.role: Only cell, generation, and sender task are attested

evidence.label: Control scope
evidence.explanation: CallerIdentity establishes local origin/lifetime, not measured software identity or device boot state.

evidence.label: Execution path
evidence.explanation: A compromised or substituted AP can issue the same narrow sign command unless the RoT independently authenticates a board-bound measured AP endpoint.

evidence.label: Required change
evidence.explanation: Separate kernel-attested service authorization from RoT-verified platform authorization. Define immutable AP boot measurement, device-pair binding/authenticated channel, accepted measurement/policy epochs, lifecycle, debug, and RMA behavior. Never trust an AP self-asserted attested=true bit.

optionalProperties.phase_gate: Board design must establish a non-circular AP boot-to-RoT chain before production-provider qualification; SPI connectivity and CallerIdentity alone never pass.

findings.title: Anti-rollback readiness compares consistent assertions rather than a protected monotonic fact
findings.summary: Readiness compares provider-reported booleans/epoch with a MACed two-slot host journal. Replaying an old journal together with an old or unauthenticated provider assessment keeps values consistent and may yield Ready. A lone valid slot is accepted, and journal-key custody is unspecified.

locations.role: Single slot and coherent pair acceptance

evidence.label: Broken control
evidence.explanation: Epoch equality detects rollback only if the provider value is fresh, authenticated, and rooted in monotonic protected state.

evidence.label: Authorization impact
evidence.explanation: A false Ready state sets remote_allowed and permits relay identity use.

evidence.label: Required change
evidence.explanation: Specify protected monotonic authorities, journal-key derivation, fresh authenticated health, atomic commit order, power-loss recovery, endurance/exhaustion, firmware/policy minima, key generation, and RMA. Do not reuse the OpenTitan lifecycle transition-attempt counter as the application epoch.

optionalProperties.phase_gate: Lifecycle cannot report Ready until replay of one/both slots and health replies, old firmware, torn writes, resets, clones, exhaustion, and RMA outcomes all fail closed against independent protected state.

findings.title: Certificate issuance and atomic key/certificate rotation are missing as a phase
findings.summary: ADR-0005 makes a managed-CA certificate and exact SPKI-derived NodeId part of authorization, but the proposed sequence jumps to service-net mTLS without explicit enrollment/binding. Key activation, CSR issuance, certificate installation, NodeId change, old-certificate revocation, and rollback state require a staged atomic lifecycle.

evidence.label: Missing prerequisite
evidence.explanation: Current KMS metadata cannot represent P-256 SPKI/NodeId, certificate serial/chain reference, active key generation, or enrollment state.

evidence.label: Unsafe intermediate state
evidence.explanation: Activating a key before its certificate causes outage; retaining generations without typed binding can select the wrong identity.

evidence.label: Required change
evidence.explanation: Add protected-key CSR proof-of-possession, CA profile validation, exact SPKI DER/NodeId check, atomic staged-to-active tuple, renewal overlap, revocation distribution, crash recovery, and RMA replacement. Private scalar import remains forbidden.

optionalProperties.phase_gate: mTLS integration waits until the leaf validates under the configured client CA, its P-256 SPKI matches the provider key, its extension equals SHA-256(SPKI DER), and signing names that active generation.

findings.title: Production selection must cover the whole artifact, not a provider boolean
findings.summary: KMS currently trusts provider-reported production_capable and does not intrinsically reject SiloWrapped; service-net separately accepts a tls-insecure build. Provider-only compile-time separation cannot prove that a product image lacks all development and downgrade paths.

evidence.label: Provider downgrade
evidence.explanation: A SiloWrapped adapter reporting production_capable=true is not hard-rejected by RootAssessment.

evidence.label: TLS downgrade
evidence.explanation: The feature guard rejects conflicts but deliberately accepts tls-insecure alone.

evidence.label: Required change
evidence.explanation: One production product profile must compile-error on DEV_REFERENCE/Silo/TestHooks/software signing, tls-insecure, raw/K1 relay, both/neither provider, or unverified TLS; runtime must fail on absent hardware or trust material.

optionalProperties.phase_gate: Pass only when artifact-level evidence shows exactly one hardware provider and verified TLS flavor, no forbidden symbols/manifests/routes, and no fallback under provider/credential failure.

findings.title: Service-net authorization must bind the live cell generation, not only the service name or TID
findings.summary: The current durable broker pattern stores cell_id, generation, and service TID and checks them against the live registry. By contrast, the simpler supervisor authorization only validates caller presence and live TID. A signing path modeled on the latter can accept an old queued request after restart/TID reuse because the trailer's generation is never compared. Identity signing needs its own live service-net binding and invalidation semantics.

locations.role: TID-only supervisor pattern unsuitable for signing
Generation exists specifically to distinguish respawns

evidence.label: Attacker-controlled source
evidence.explanation: A request queued by a prior service-net generation retains the old kernel-attested generation and possibly a later-reused numeric TID.

evidence.label: Broken control
evidence.explanation: Checking only sender against sys_lookup_service(NET) ignores the generation evidence intended to prevent authority inheritance.

evidence.label: Required change
evidence.explanation: Add explicit service-net registration/binding that records cell_id, generation, service TID, binding epoch, active identity generation, and policy epoch. Revalidate the live NET registry and all stored fields on every sign request; invalidate outstanding requests and responses on restart, rotation, or policy change.

optionalProperties.phase_gate: Authorization tests must deny no/forged trailer, broker, supervisor signing, arbitrary cell, stale generation, reused TID, stale binding epoch, post-rotation request, and delayed response; only the current service-net generation may request the typed TLS signature.

findings.title: Repairing Silo before removing its direct public API creates an alternate signing boundary
findings.summary: The existing Silo service accepts requests from any sender, and the public handle exposes init_key, generic sign, ECDH, and raw opcodes. Merely making the guest boot would activate a path that bypasses KMS policy and contradicts the sole-service-net-caller architecture. It would also contaminate QEMU evidence because successful signing would not prove policy mediation.

locations.role: Public seed and generic sign operations
Arbitrary non-hypervisor cell initializes the key

evidence.label: Attacker-controlled source
evidence.explanation: Any cell can resolve Silo and send raw requests because sys_recv(0) accepts all senders.

evidence.label: Dangerous sink
evidence.explanation: Those requests reach protected P-256 signing and caller-provided key initialization without KMS authorization.

evidence.label: Required change
evidence.explanation: The reference repair must make KMS the only attested Silo caller, delete production/public SiloHandle methods and raw opcode exposure, eliminate caller-supplied production seeds, and exclude the entire service from production artifacts. A reference-only deterministic seed may exist only behind an unmistakable DEV_REFERENCE build and cannot count as custody evidence.

optionalProperties.phase_gate: Reference-Silo phase fails until direct calls from the test cell, service-net, broker, supervisor, and arbitrary cells deny; the only successful route is service-net → attested KMS policy → DEV_REFERENCE adapter, and evidence is labeled non-hardware-qualified.

findings.title: The SPI command profile lacks a specified freshness, reset, and response-correlation contract
findings.summary: A narrow opcode set is not replay protection. On a physical SPI boundary, captured commands/responses, delayed frames, device resets, AP resets, and concurrent requests can replay stale health/epoch/public-key state or misassociate a signature. The current Silo mailbox increments a sequence and the guest echoes it, but the host does not validate the echoed sequence, illustrating why a field without enforced semantics is insufficient.

locations.role: Sequence is generated and allowed to wrap
Response is consumed without checking echoed sequence
Research identifies SPI replay, substitution, reset, and narrow-profile requirements

evidence.label: Broken control
evidence.explanation: A monotonically changing or echoed identifier gives no freshness if the verifier does not enforce uniqueness, boot-session scope, command binding, and authenticated integrity.

evidence.label: Impact
evidence.explanation: Replayed health/epoch material can feed readiness; mismatched signatures cause availability failures; replayed commands can consume finite signer/entropy/transport resources.

evidence.label: Required change
evidence.explanation: Freeze canonical request/response framing with version, exact opcode, identity generation, policy epoch, AP/RoT boot-session nonces, monotonic request ID, request digest, status, length, and authenticated integrity. Bind each response to the full request, self-verify signatures, reject duplicates/out-of-window frames, and force re-attestation after either side resets.

optionalProperties.phase_gate: Simulation/FPGA gate must inject duplicate, reordered, truncated, bit-flipped, delayed, cross-reset, wraparound, timeout, cancellation, and concurrent frames; every case fails closed without stale readiness or misassociated signature.

findings.title: The existing root ABI conflates a 32-byte X25519 node identity with the new P-256 certificate identity
findings.summary: The one-provider-seam direction is sound, but the current seam and public status are shaped around a single 32-byte key and static X25519 DH, while ADR-0005 requires a P-256 SPKI/certificate and P-256 signing. Simply evolving the trait risks generic key IDs, wrong-purpose key selection, or falsely treating a P-256-only OpenTitan signer as satisfying the existing C2C identity lifecycle.

locations.role: Single 32-byte OpenedRoot and untyped root operations
Existing ABI is acquire plus X25519 DH
Status publishes only one 32-byte public key
Existing DH is fixed to KMS_NODE_KEY_ID_C2C

evidence.label: Incompatible contracts
evidence.explanation: A P-256 uncompressed SEC1 public key is 65 bytes and ADR identity is the complete SPKI DER hash; neither fits the current [u8; 32] field.

evidence.label: Security risk
evidence.explanation: Caller-selected generic handles/key IDs encourage cross-purpose use; a coarse provider-ready state can authorize TLS even when only the unrelated C2C key is healthy, or vice versa.

evidence.label: Required change
evidence.explanation: Keep one ProtectedRootProvider implementation boundary but expose typed leaf capabilities and independent readiness: C2C X25519 and relay TLS P-256 must have fixed algorithms, purposes, handles/generations, public encodings, and authorization policies. The SPI profile should implement only the production-required P-256 TLS capability and must not pretend to support X25519.

optionalProperties.phase_gate: Contract gate must decide and version the ABI before callers migrate; tests reject cross-purpose handles, algorithms, generations, public-key encodings, and readiness substitution.

findings.title: The phase order freezes contracts before two feasibility decisions that can change them
findings.summary: The proposed order starts with contracts and repairs Silo before proving that embedded-tls 0.19 supports an external protected client-auth signer, and postpones the concrete OpenTitan silicon/firmware/transport/secure-NVM/board trust decision. If either assumption fails, the frozen API and lifecycle model will be wrong; the prohibited escape hatches are filesystem PEM or a software signer.

locations.role: Current provider has no client certificate or signer
mTLS profile and lifecycle are blocked prerequisites
Concrete production release, SPI profile, board binding, and rollback design remain selections

evidence.label: TLS feasibility risk
evidence.explanation: Current CryptoProvider explicitly keeps default signer/client_cert behavior; no demonstrated asynchronous/external CertificateVerify hook exists in the reviewed code.

evidence.label: Hardware feasibility risk
evidence.explanation: OpenTitan master/reference APIs, FPGA evidence, and stock boards do not identify a purchasable qualified product, pinned firmware ABI, monotonic storage design, provisioning service, or AP boot binding.

evidence.label: Required change
evidence.explanation: Add a Phase -1 decision gate: prove the TLS library can drive TLS 1.3 client auth through the typed callback without key bytes, and select/pin the production RoT part, firmware release, one SPI profile, protected NVM strategy, provisioning/lifecycle support, and board threat model. Then freeze contracts.

optionalProperties.phase_gate: No contract freeze or Silo repair until both throwaway feasibility proofs pass. Failure requires an explicit TLS provider or hardware architecture decision, never PEM/software fallback or scope reduction.

coverage_summary: VERDICT: CONDITIONAL NO-GO. The architectural direction—one KMS-owned ProtectedRootProvider, service-net-only TLS signing, DEV_REFERENCE-only QEMU Silo, and a hardware-gated OpenTitan-compatible P-256 provider—is sound, and the current tree remains fail-closed because runtime KMS uses UnavailableRootProvider and broker relay exhaustion returns NotSupported. The proposed sequence is not yet safe or plan-ready: 7 High and 3 Medium design findings survive. Required phase order/gates: (0) threat-model and feasibility gate: prove embedded-tls external TLS 1.3 client-auth signing without key bytes; select and pin actual RoT silicon/firmware, exactly one SPI profile, protected-NVM strategy, provisioning support, AP boot-binding design, and board threat model; (1) contract/product gate: version typed C2C-vs-TLS capabilities, freeze a TLS CertificateVerify-only envelope, service-net generation binding, canonical/authenticated SPI framing, and a whole-artifact production profile that excludes Silo/TestHooks/software signing/tls-insecure/raw/K1; (2) KMS policy/lifecycle gate: implement independently protected monotonic state, fresh authenticated health, journal-key custody, atomic power-fail-safe lifecycle, key-purpose separation, audit/error precedence, rotation/RMA/exhaustion behavior, with signing still disabled; (3) DEV_REFERENCE Silo gate: repair artifact/init only behind KMS, remove direct/raw/public Silo signing and caller-supplied production seed paths, enforce freshness/correlation, and label all evidence software-only; (4) certificate enrollment/binding gate: protected-key CSR proof-of-possession, managed-CA profile, exact P-256 SPKI and NodeId extension binding, staged activation/renewal/revocation/recovery; (5) service-net mTLS gate: CA/hostname validation, typed protected signer, bounded timeout/cancellation/concurrency, no private bytes or fallback; (6) QEMU relay evidence gate: complete negative authorization, stale-generation, mismatch, outage, and downgrade cases plus two-node opaque Noise evidence, explicitly non-production; (7) OpenTitan simulation/FPGA gate: hardware-backed/sideloaded P-256, authenticated freshness/reset protocol, rollback fault injection, pinned firmware ABI; (8) board design/provisioning gate: production part, schematic, AP-to-RoT measured boot binding, reset/power/bus/entropy/debug/lifecycle/manufacturing controls; (9) production hardware qualification gate: physical non-extractability, rollback, clone, update/RMA, latency/load and artifact-selection evidence; only then (10) production two-node ADR-0005 qualification. Current RPi3/EL1 is excluded from Silo production evidence, and QEMU/FPGA results may never clear hardware gates. No code, tests, builds, network calls, or edits were performed, as required.
